title: Fixture enrichment boundary — operator-locked at draft
body:
The fixture is enriched ONLY to address the three concrete fairness gaps surfaced by the parent dogfood (Plan 003 close-out commit `616ad94`, findings F2C-E008 + auditor-overlay-001 + auditor-overlay-002):

**(1) Adapter / source modules.** Include all relevant adapter sources from `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/runtime_evidence/`: `web.py`, `ios.py`, `android.py`, `backend.py`, `harness.py`, plus any minimal config / shared base modules required to interpret them (e.g. `__init__.py` if it carries shared types or base classes the adapters extend). The bar is 'fair representation of the Plan G surface as a cross-vendor auditor would expect to see it,' not exhaustive shipping of every file under `runtime_evidence/`.

**(2) Runtime-like artifacts per source.** For each adapter, at least one runtime-like artifact:
- web — screenshot.png (placeholder), dom-dump.html, console.json (sample), network.har (sample)
- ios — screenshot.png (placeholder), log-slice.txt, crash-marker.txt OR no-crash.txt
- android — screenshot.png (placeholder), logcat-slice.txt, tombstone-marker.txt OR no-tombstone.txt
- backend — log.jsonl request sample, response.jsonl sample
- harness — runner-output.txt or similar invocation artifact
Synthetic / stub-quality artifacts are acceptable. Operator pre-approves stubs since the fixture is for the auditor's pattern-matching, not real session capture.

**(3) Plan G read-only invariant (D006 carry-forward from Plan 003 D001).** Plan G's plan dir (`docs/plans/2026-05-06-001-feat-goal-governance/`) stays untouched. Artifacts are COPIED into this plan's evidence fixture under `docs/plans/2026-05-07-002-…/evidence/g-mirror/`, never moved or symlinked.

**Why locked at draft:** the parent dogfood's fairness gaps are concrete and bounded; without this lock the F001 implementer could drift into 'enrich until codex agrees' which is the same anti-pattern as matcher tuning (D002). Bounding the additive surface to these three categories keeps the dogfood honest.

**How to apply:** F001 step 2 builds the fixture from Plan 003's existing mirror; steps 3–4 add ONLY the three D001 categories. Acceptance #1 verifies the diff is confined to those categories. Anything else is scope creep → revert from this plan + queue separately.

title: Cost discipline — exactly one live codex invocation; success ≠ clean PASS
body:
Operator-locked at draft.

**Budget:** Exactly ONE live codex invocation in this plan. Any second invocation requires explicit operator approval BEFORE the call is made. Cited precedent: Plan 003 D009 — implementer-side mistake added a redundant Step 1 close-without-override that re-invoked codex live (~$1 wasted), recorded as a process failure.

**Acceptance redefinition:** 'parsed live envelope + classified findings + close/override path exercised', NOT 'clean PASS'. A `disagree` envelope with classified follow-ups is a SUCCESSFUL outcome of this plan. The plan flips passes:true regardless of whether codex agreed; the value is the recorded honest decision, not a particular verdict.

**Three release valves forbidden by default:**
- **Matcher tuning** to force a pass. The fixture's `objective_contract.json.required_evidence` list stays byte-identical to Plan 003's. Asserted by acceptance #2.
- **F2 module patches** in this plan. Default response to a real platform issue (D005 bucket (a)) is a queued follow-up plan. Tiny patches require explicit operator approval BEFORE edit. Asserted by D004 worktree boundary + acceptance #9.
- **Prompt template tuning.** Default is parser-only (carry-forward from parser plan D006). Asserted by D004 worktree boundary.

**Why locked at draft:** the parent dogfood ran into a parser defect that took 3 codex invocations to surface (initial audit + redundant Step 1 + Step 2 with override). Now that the parser is fixed, the marginal cost of a clean second run is justified IF the first run reveals something un-recoverable (e.g. dispatch_response_malformed, escape clause D007). But the default policy is single-shot.

**How to apply:** F001 step 7 is THE live invocation. Steps 1–6 are local-only setup. Step 8+ are post-call analysis with no further codex calls. If a (a) or (b) finding triggers a tempting in-plan patch, the implementer surfaces the temptation as a D-entry and waits for explicit operator approval before patching.

title: Cross-vendor invariant preserved (carry-forward)
body:
Carry-forward from Goal Governance V1 §5 / Plan F2 D003 / Plan 003 D003.

Same-vendor refusal stays default. NO `DONTPANIC_GOAL_AUDITOR_ALLOW_SAME_VENDOR=1` is set in this plan. The auditor must be codex (different vendor than implementer=claude) by F1's resolver default.

**Verified at envelope level (acceptance #5):**
- `envelope.auditor_agent == 'codex'`
- `envelope.implementer_agent == 'claude'`
- `os.environ.get('DONTPANIC_GOAL_AUDITOR_ALLOW_SAME_VENDOR')` is unset at invocation time

**Why:** this is the load-bearing property of the entire cross-vendor adversarial-review story. Allowing same-vendor in this plan would render the dogfood scientifically meaningless. The operator's deliberate override env exists for emergency operator workflows, NOT for dogfood plans.

**How to apply:** F001 step 7 invokes codex through the production path; the resolver enforces this automatically. Step 9 asserts the three properties above against the captured envelope.

title: Worktree boundary — this plan dir only
body:
Worktree-boundary invariant verified at commit time.

**Permitted writes:**
- Anywhere under `docs/plans/2026-05-07-002-fix-cross-vendor-dogfood-fixture-runtime-artifacts/` (this plan dir, including `evidence/g-mirror/` fixture tree, `evidence/plan-closeout-memo.md`, decisions.jsonl updates, features.json passes flip).

**Forbidden writes:**
- `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/` — ALL submodules. No F2 module changes (`completion_dispatch.py`, `completion_auditor.py`, `completion_gate.py`, `cli.py`, `supervisor.py`, etc.). No F1 surface (`sufficiency_auditor.py`, `sufficiency_gate.py`). No `runtime_evidence/` adapter changes. No `executors/` changes. No test code changes. No additions under `tests/fixtures/` (parser plan's territory, frozen).
- `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/prompts/completion_audit_prompt.md` — prompt template untouched (carry-forward from parser plan D006).
- `claude/shared/` — agent-conventions subtree.
- All other plan dirs read-only:
  - `docs/plans/2026-05-06-001-feat-goal-governance/` (Plan G — source corpus per D006)
  - `docs/plans/2026-05-06-002-feat-post-impl-completion-audit/` (Plan F2)
  - `docs/plans/2026-05-06-003-fix-live-cross-vendor-goal-audit-dogfood/` (Plan 003 — parent dogfood)
  - `docs/plans/2026-05-07-001-fix-completion-dispatch-codex-stream-parser/` (parser plan)
  - all other docs/plans/* dirs

**Why:** a dogfood that drifts into module-code mutation is no longer a dogfood — it becomes implicit v2 platform work. The boundary keeps the dogfood honest: this plan ONLY records what the now-correct system says about a fair fixture. Real platform fixes flow through proper plan channels.

**Release valve:** if codex's parsed findings include a (D005-bucket-a) real platform issue that the operator deems tiny + worth fixing in-plan, the implementer surfaces the proposed patch as a D-entry, waits for explicit operator approval, then proceeds. The default response is queued follow-up.

**How to apply:** F001 step 12 runs `git diff --name-only HEAD` and asserts the diff is confined to this plan dir. Anything else → revert from this commit and re-scope.

title: Finding-classification taxonomy — 4-bucket, carry-forward from Plan 003 D005
body:
Each codex `finding_disposition` returned by the live invocation is classified through the 4-bucket taxonomy locked in Plan 003 D005:

**(a) real platform issue** — codex's disposition flags a genuine F2 / parser / dispatcher / auditor defect that affects correctness or operator trust.
→ Default response: queued follow-up plan with concrete slug suggestion.
→ In-plan patch ONLY if tiny + operator-approved (D002 release valve).

**(b) prompt-tuning gap** — codex's disposition reflects a real ambiguity in the auditor prompt that a parser-only fix cannot address. The disposition is correct given current prompt; codex's confusion is the operator's signal.
→ Default: queued follow-up plan; in-plan prompt edit forbidden by D002.

**(c) spec-clarification** — codex's disposition is correct given current spec but reflects vocabulary / matcher convention drift between the contract's `required_evidence` strings and the auditor's natural language. Not a defect.
→ Record + dismiss. Rationale documented in close-out memo.

**(d) false-positive** — codex's disposition is incorrect (e.g. citing a non-existent path, misreading the contract, hallucinating a coverage claim).
→ Record + dismiss. Rationale documented.

**Per-finding decision recorded** in decisions.jsonl (one D-entry per ship, with embedded per-finding tag table). The classification IS the work product; whether codex agreed or disagreed is secondary.

**Why locked at draft:** without this taxonomy, the implementer would face a binary 'agree-or-disagree' decision and lose the nuance. The 4-bucket vocabulary is what makes the dogfood produce queueable signal rather than vague friction.

**How to apply:** F001 step 10 walks each `findings_dispositions[i]` and tags it. Step 11 chooses the close path based on the tag distribution (D007). Acceptance #6 asserts every disposition has a tag.

title: Plan G is the source corpus — read-only (carry-forward)
body:
Carry-forward from Plan 003 D001.

Plan G's plan dir (`docs/plans/2026-05-06-001-feat-goal-governance/`) stays read-only across the lifecycle of this plan. Artifacts (source modules, runtime-like artifacts, contract / features / decisions) are COPIED into this plan's `evidence/g-mirror/` fixture, never moved or symlinked. Plan G's frozen history is the canonical reference; this plan's mirror is an enrichment-only copy.

**Why:** Plan G is signed-off (commit `0715bc7`); editing its plan dir to make it more dogfood-friendly would corrupt the historical record. The mirror pattern (copy-into-fixture) preserves both Plan G's freeze AND the dogfood's freedom to enrich.

**How to apply:** F001 step 2 verifies Plan G plan dir is unchanged at sequence start. Step 12 (worktree boundary) re-verifies at commit time. If any reason emerges to edit Plan G itself, that's a separate plan with its own discussion.

title: Close-path discipline — three honest paths + one escape clause
body:
Plan close goes through one of THREE honest paths based on the parsed envelope, plus ONE escape clause:

**Path 1 — Envelope `status='agree'`** → close without override.
→ Suspicious if first run; codex rarely agrees with v1 verbatim. Investigate carefully before accepting. Possible if v1 correctly captured the gap shape AND codex agreed on severity/disposition for every finding.
→ Acceptance evidence: envelope.json + transcript + close-out memo recording 'no override needed; all dispositions agree:true'.

**Path 2 — Envelope `status='disagree'`, all findings classified (c)/(d)** → close with override; reason = classified findings summary.
→ Override.json carries all 4 D004 hashes (features + objective_contract + completion_findings + evidence_manifest); reason text includes per-finding (c)/(d) tags + dismissal rationale.
→ Acceptance evidence: envelope.json + transcript + override.json with hashes + close-out memo recording the classification table.

**Path 3 — Envelope `status='disagree'`, any finding classified (a)/(b)** → close with override; reason = follow-up plan citation.
→ Override.json carries all 4 D004 hashes; reason text cites the queued follow-up plan slug(s) for each (a)/(b) finding. The override is the deliberate operator choice — the follow-up captures the real work; the override unblocks THIS plan from staying open indefinitely.
→ Acceptance evidence: envelope.json + transcript + override.json + close-out memo + new follow-up plan slugs added to memo's queued-followups list.

**Escape clause — Envelope `status='dispatch_response_malformed'`** → STOP, escalate, no flip.
→ This would mean the parser plan (`2026-05-07-001`, ship `080b907`) didn't fully solve the format gap. Surface a new D-entry recording the unexpected output shape. Do NOT close with override (that would silently mask a regression in the parser-fix's claimed property).
→ Expected NOT to fire. Parser plan's tests cover the dogfood transcript shape directly + 12 edge cases; if it fires, it indicates a codex output format the parser tests didn't anticipate.

**Why locked at draft:** without this enumeration, the implementer might default to 'override = workaround' framing and treat any non-agree as a failure. The taxonomy makes 'override = deliberate operator choice' explicit. It also makes the malformed case un-overridable, preventing parser regressions from being papered over.

**How to apply:** F001 step 8 verifies envelope.status is in {'agree','disagree'} (escape clause check). Step 11 chooses the close path based on classification tag distribution from step 10. Acceptance #7 asserts the chosen path is recorded with all required artifacts (override.json with 4 hashes if used).
